key_insight: A microstructure-conditioned hybrid physics-data surrogate can accurately predict multiscale behavior of mycelium composites with far less data, enabling optimization across varying microstructures.
engineering_relevance: This makes functionally graded multiscale design practical for sustainable materials by linking manufacturing and microstructure choices to target structural performance.
method: Use a hybrid physics-data surrogate for microscale mechanics.
Condition the model on microstructural variables via a hypernetwork.
Extend conditioning to manufacturing variables for direct process-to-property optimization.
evidence_signal: Validated against full FE^2 simulation and used to optimize a graded multiscale disk, reducing peak stress by 42% versus a random microstructure.
watch_item: Performance may depend on the representativeness of the limited training data and on how well the chosen microstructural/manufacturing variables capture real process variability.
paper_title: Microstructure-Conditioned Surrogate Models for Graded Multiscale Optimization of Mycelium Composites
